9e3554df42a99c90d41b0c153adfd018beeeb3d2 is the last commit on this lane that changes anything outside docs/06_status/proof/UTV2-1889/. It supersedes c4f22cc3117387dca5edd1e73ae66bb676ab9fa0, which was this field's value while the operator-attestation route was still in the tree. The anchor is moved rather than its claim reworded, on the same standard this note has applied to every previous anchor: an anchor carries the binding claim 'every later commit touches only the proof directory or carries main's files forward', and a commit that changes lane source falsifies it.
The lane's source-changing commits are: 4701685541 (the original seven files, including the operator-attestation CLI that is now removed -- the design is preserved there), 2b0a01e02 (the cross-file coupling test, since removed with its subject), f767e81ab (the SGO journey proof), b22617cae (the repair of gaps A, B and D in apps/ingestor/src/results-resolver.ts), 9a2b45786 (the staging journey and the one-line package.json wiring entry), c4f22cc31 (namespacing the fixture's event name), and 9e3554df42a99c90d41b0c153adfd018beeeb3d2 (removing the operator route, taking `operator` out of the trust allow-list, and correcting the failure-6 explanation). unit_tests.label: The stats aggregate, the report adapter and the ten integrated SGO journey tests. Down from 50 at 8c57fc3f4: the fifteen tests whose subject was the operator-attestation CLI (its planner, its --help anti-drift control, its parseCli and entrypoint tests, and the writer/reader coupling assertion between that CLI and the grading pass) are removed with the CLI itself at 9e3554df42a99c90d41b0c153adfd018beeeb3d2. The journey tests run the real SGO parser (fetchSGOResults with an injected fetchImpl, so the provider is never contacted), the real resolveAndInsertResults, the real processSubmission, the real runGradingPass and the real computeTrackOnlyStats against seeded participants, events and event_participants. The read-side classifyResultProvenance tests keep an `operator` fixture because that function reports a row's provenance by name and is not a trust decision. 9 pre-existing tests in this file are untouched.

Moneyline grading from an ingested win flag, the result-market-key guard, provider-keyed provenance, and the composed Track Only + SGO moneyline journey. Up from 82 at 8c57fc3f4: the provenance-crossing test is replaced by two -- `operator provenance is refused: the deferred attestation route has no trust entry` (event_provenance_untrusted_provider) and `provenance is keyed by provider: sgo may not borrow another source` (event_provenance_invalid_ingestion_cycle) -- and the restrictToPickIds tests from 9a2b45786 remain. Every moneyline fixture now carries `sgo` / `ingestor.cycle` provenance, the only provenance that ships. The 71 pre-existing tests are the population UTV2-1886 left green and all still pass.

The gap A/B/D repair, asserted on the resolver itself. The five new tests pin: a moneyline writes one row per side keyed game_moneyline_win with the team's participant_id and a value in {1,0} (and assert directly that neither raw score, 5 or 3, reaches an outcome-keyed row); a tie writes 0.5 on both sides; a half-scored event writes NOTHING and counts skippedMoneylineOutcomeUnresolved; an event with no event_participants rows -- the exact shape of the 3,000+ historical game-line rows -- writes NOTHING and counts skippedTeamSideUnresolved; and a game total is untouched by the moneyline path. The 4 pre-existing UTV2-1287 telemetry tests are unchanged and still pass.

The ingestor suite, including test 76 ('results-resolver canonical alias maps include expanded player props and game lines'), which was the one collateral failure of the gap A repair and is the reason it is recorded here. It asserted the sixteen <league>-<bet>-all-game aliases that gap A removed as unreachable by construction. It was not deleted: it now asserts the two keys normalizeSgoProviderMarketKey can actually emit AND that three of the removed keys resolve to undefined, so silently re-adding an unreachable alias fails. The 28 player-prop alias assertions above it are untouched.

The whole wired ops suite, 21 files, 98.8s, run at 9e3554df42a99c90d41b0c153adfd018beeeb3d2. 3106 rather than the 3121 recorded at 8c57fc3f4: the difference is exactly the fifteen operator-CLI tests removed from scripts/ops/track-only-report.test.ts. Recorded because the journey tests live in the already-wired track-only-report.test.ts rather than a new file -- pnpm verify fails closed with WIRING_TEST_UNWIRED_NEW on an unwired scripts/ test. A first run of this suite at this tree reported 4 failures; they were the exact signature of mutation stats-4 (`a loss costs nothing`), because the mutation battery was editing stats.ts concurrently. The suite was re-run alone and is recorded from that clean run; the contaminated one is named here rather than dropped.

coverage_gap.correction: The previous text of this block asserted two things that are now refuted by execution rather than by argument. It said a live suite here 'would prove that the seed it just wrote can be read back, not that the journey works', and it named a production operator attestation as the action that closes the gap. Both were wrong, and the reasoning error is nameable: it conflated seeding a game_moneyline_win ROW with seeding a provider PAYLOAD. The suite seeds neither result rows nor settlements. It hands the real SGO parser a provider payload and then asserts what the real resolver, the real submission path, the real grading pass and the real stats aggregate do with it against real PostgREST. A production operator attestation is therefore not the only way, and was not the way, this gap closed.

coverage_gap.isolation: Every row the suite writes is namespaced by CI_FIXTURE_RUN_ID (utv2-1630-34713309743-1 on this run), carried on the provider event id, both team external ids AND the event name. The event name is load-bearing, and the first staging run of this suite (34700508935 attempt 1, 4 pass / 2 fail) showed why -- but the mechanism recorded here at 8c57fc3f4 was wrong and is corrected from measurement. It said grading `never cross-checks the participants`; that is too broad, and PM's review said so. apps/api/src/grading-service.ts resolvePickEvent DOES filter candidate events by the pick's participant (eventParticipants.listByParticipant) before chooseEventForPick orders by name and start-time proximity. The actual mechanism was upstream of grading: computeSubmissionIdempotencyKey in apps/api/src/submission-service.ts hashes source | market | selection | line | odds | eventName and NOT metadata, so two fixtures differing only in participant ids and provider event id hashed to one key and processSubmission returned the fully-scored run's existing pick -- there was no second pick, and the settlement the test read was that pick's genuine settlement. Read-only staging SQL confirms it: run 34700508935-1 holds exactly one pick (fd6423fe), whose teamId is the main fixture's AWAY participant and whose settlement is against the main event. Namespacing the event name fixed it because the name is a key input; namespacing the id alone was not isolation.
coverage_gap.target_control: scripts/ci/assert-staging-target.ts is called in the suite's before() hook and refuses a production, unknown, ambiguous or unresolvable target. The credentialed job separately asserts CI_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF == xskgrzbteyqdufktjrjx before any test runs.
coverage_gap.zero_skips_is_enforced_not_observed: When CI_FIXTURE_RUN_ID is present the suite sets mustRun and refuses to skip: a missing credential or an unapproved target fails the tests rather than silently reporting them as skipped. Verified both ways locally before this run -- with no staging target the suite reports 6 skipped / 0 fail, and with CI_FIXTURE_RUN_ID set against a bad target it reports 0 skipped / 6 fail.
coverage_gap.grading_population_restriction: runGradingPass gained an optional restrictToPickIds set, applied AFTER the normal population read as an intersection. It can only remove candidates, never admit one the population did not already return, which is what keeps this suite from sweeping and settling staging's unrelated backlog. Mutation-tested three ways: ignoring the restriction fails two tests, and using it as a union or admission path fails the 'cannot admit' test specifically.

what_remains_unproven: PRODUCTION: nothing in this lane ran against production. No production row was written, and no production claim is made. The only production reads are the governed read-only SELECT recorded under static_proof.production_measurement.

PRODUCTION: ambiguous-event resolution. A pick without an explicit event id resolves to the nearest participant-linked event by name and start time; whether that is always the intended event for real submissions is not proven here and is a production-acceptance check, not a fixture question.

PRODUCTION: real SGO ingestion. The resolver is exercised with a recorded provider payload through an injected transport; the provider was never contacted, SGO remains parked, and no ingestion cycle ran.

BROWSER: no browser interface is exercised by this suite. The Smart Form e2e suite asserts the persisted pick in memory and its CI gate defaults off; browser authentication and the Smart Form HTTP/controller path are evidenced only there.
SCALE: the suite proves one Track Only moneyline through the journey against staging. It is not a repeatability claim and not a statistics claim over a real cohort.
coverage_gap.guard_state: No containment setting was changed. SGO remains parked, member delivery remains off, no operator write route ships, and this suite writes only namespaced fixture rows to staging.
coverage_gap.ambiguous_event_limitation: Separate, and kept visible rather than closed by fixture naming: when a pick carries no explicit event id, resolvePickEvent chooses among the pick's participant-linked events by name match and then by start-time proximity, so with two participant-linked events on adjacent dates and an ambiguous name it selects the NEAREST rather than an explicit canonical event. Namespacing the fixture name is isolation for this suite, not a production resolution repair. This is a production-acceptance item and is listed under what_remains_unproven.
